purpose: Every numeric threshold used by the deterministic feasibility engine (J6). Kept out of code so it is reviewable, diffable and owned by policy rather than by a developer.

provenance.note: The anchor specifications do NOT source these numbers. They are engineering defaults chosen to be conservative and are marked provisional so that an actuarial/product owner can replace them without touching J6. Every FeasibilityResult echoes the policy version and the thresholds actually used, so historical results stay interpretable if the policy changes.
provenance.owner: unassigned - needs a named product/actuarial owner
provenance.review_by: before any production or regulated use

max_savings_rate.rationale: Caps how much of net monthly income may be committed to a single new goal, leaving headroom for irregular months. 40% is deliberately conservative; a higher ratio makes goals look feasible that fail in a bad month.

emergency_months_required.rationale: Minimum liquid runway before a new goal may be considered feasible. Below 4 months a new commitment converts a shock into a crisis.

emergency_basis_months.rationale: Denominator convention for converting an emergency corpus into a runway figure. Conventional 6-month guidance.

seasonal_stress_ratio.rationale: When the worst observed month is below this fraction of the average, the goal is additionally stress-tested against the worst month rather than the average. Prevents seasonal and irregular earners from being approved against a flattering mean.

income_smoothing_window_months.rationale: Trailing window for income aggregation. 12 months captures at least one full seasonal cycle; a 3-month window hides off-season collapse.

debt_service_ceiling.rationale: Total debt service above this share of income marks a debt-spiral profile and blocks new commitments regardless of apparent savings capacity.

debt_to_income_spiral_ratio.rationale: Outstanding debt above this multiple of monthly income marks a debt-spiral profile. Chosen over an interest-rate proxy because a long-tenor loan carries a low monthly payment while still being structurally unaffordable - the monthly-service test alone approved the debt-spiral persona in testing.

emergency_basis_amount.rationale: Household monthly essential outflow used as the numerator for runway. Derived from the persona's recurring essential commitments, not a market constant, so it belongs to feasibility policy rather than to the external-benchmark file.

protection_requires_insurance.rationale: A pure savings reserve cannot absorb a large acute medical shock. If the customer's stated mechanism for a protection objective is savings-only, the construct is judged wrong-construct and challenged, even when a feasible alternative exists.
protection_requires_insurance.source: Anchor 1 §4 Challenge definition; J7 healthcare-reserve demo scenario
